author: Zara Barker
title: Sorrento Valley dog poisoned with metal hooks in meat thrown in his backyard - NewsBreak
text:
By Zara Barker ,
26 minutes ago
SAN DIEGO (FOX 5/KUSI) — A Sorrento Valley homeowner is searching for answers after her dog was poisoned by tainted meat in their backyard.
“Our safe haven is really our backyard, and Bruno loves his backyard,” Sabrina Bazzo said. But that sense of safety and security in her own yard was shattered on Friday.
Sabrina Bazzo, who is also on the San Diego Unified School Board, said she let her 2-year-old Golden Retriever Bruno outside in their backyard when she got home, and noticed Bruno was chewing on something. She went outside and found two bundles of meat, tied with a string, with blue poison and metal hooks inside.
“This is normally a very quiet neighborhood, and to know that that kind of evil just exists right around you is creepy,” Bazzo said. Her backyard only backs up to homes, meaning she believes it was one of her neighbors who tried to poison her dog.
Bazzo rushed Bruno to the vet, where they induced vomiting. They got there just in time, as Bruno threw up the rat poison and metal hooks, before it went into his intestines.
Bazzo said she’s sad and angry, and is now trying to figure out who, and why someone would do this.
“To know we have a neighbor that can go throw dangerous things in the backyard,” Bazzo said, it makes her feel scared.
In September, she received a letter, presumably from a neighbor, typed in red letters.
“It just said shut your {Go } dog up, and it was all typed so we don’t know who it was from.”
Bazzo said they never leave Bruno outside, unless they are home, so he can enjoy the backyard. The letter mentioned that the dog barks all night, but Bazzo said, “he sleeps in bed with me; he even has a bark collar that just buzzes.”
That letter was addressed to Sabrina, and her late husband, who had passed away from brain cancer just a few months before she received that letter.
“Bruno’s just really been a source of support and comfort for our entire family for a really difficult time for us, and so now to have this happen … it just adds more strain and stress,” she said.
Bazzo is now sending letters to warn her neighbors, and adding cameras to the back of her home.
The San Diego Police Department and the Humane Society are investigating.
“There’s so many other options that people can take versus taking their frustration out on an animal that is voiceless, to me it’s no different than a child, these animals have very little ways to protect themselves,” Jace Huggins, the chief of Humane Law Enforcement, said.
Huggins said his job is to protect animals from humans, and also protect humans from animals.
While Huggins can’t speak on this ongoing investigation, he wants the community to know to call them if they ever have an issue.
“Whether it be about barking, people not picking up after them …. please call us, we answer our phones 24/7.”
Poisoning could be either a misdemeanor or a felony.
